transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-11
Start: 10:00 UTC
Duration: 78 minutes (approx)
Location: Zoom / company-wide stream
Attendees: Maya Chen, Samir Patel, Diego Ramos, Asha Kapoor, Ling Zhao + all-hands

Summary:
Quick ops cadence review, priority rotations for the next 90 days, incident retrospective highlights, and product signals that will change how we measure per-route cost. Short Q&A at the end.

Topics covered:
- Holiday on-call rotations & staffing risks
- Recent SRE incident root cause (KV cash + autoscaler interplay)
- Pricing telemetry experiment for per-route token accounting
- Dedicated capacity rollouts and customer comms cadence
- Hiring snapshot + org moves

Action items (captured during call):
- Asha to publish rotation calendar and playbook
- Ling to run post-incident blameless and share RCA notes
- Diego to provide timeline for pricing telemetry and experiments
- Samir to prioritize small runtime patch to reduce head-of-line latency on small seqs

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we'll kick off, uh, real quick. agenda is on the slide — ops cadence, incidents, product signals and then q and a.
[00:28] Samir Patel: Quick note — apologies for the brief delay, I was on a kernel thread, literally. we will keep this tight.
[00:35] Diego Ramos: I wanna jump in on the product side early — we're seeing a couple of customers who want per-route cost breakdowns, that's going to shift some priorities.
[00:48] Asha Kapoor: Yep, that ties into ops because if customers start to surface more per-route telemetry we'll need to adjust the Dedicated pricing cadence and how we expose burst capacity.
[01:05] Ling Zhao: On SRE — quick reprise of the Friday outage; root cause was interplay between autoscaler thrash and the KV cache (transcript sometimes says KV cash) warming. the autoscaler removed a node while some nodes were still handling long-lived kv caches — and we hit cold-cold miss storms.
[01:35] Speaker 1: wait, so the autoscaler killed nodes while KV cache still had active sessions?
[01:40] Ling Zhao: Essentially, yeah. There was also a scheduling jitter on the cloud provider side that delayed new nodes by a few minutes.
[01:48] Samir Patel: We have two immediate fixes: reduce aggressive scale-in windows and add a guard that waits for cache drains on critical shards. small patch first, later a safer orchestration change.
[02:07] Maya Chen: Are those fixes low risk? timeline?
[02:12] Ling Zhao: The reduce scale-in window is low risk, we can ship it on canary tonight. The cache-drain guard requires a bit more testing.
[02:22] Asha Kapoor: Ok Asha note — samir, can you prioritize a canary for tonight and let ops know the rollback plan?
[02:30] Samir Patel: Yup. I'll do the canary and we'll monitor token latencies and tail-p99.
[02:36] Diego Ramos: On pricing telemetry: we want a lightweight probe that can attribute tokens to routes, but we need to ensure performance overhead is minimal. If the telemetry adds 5-10% CPU, customers will notice.
[02:55] Ling Zhao: Can we sample? or do we do full attribution server side?
[03:00] Samir Patel: Sampling is the plan — probabilistic attribution with extrapolation. It's what the big clouds do for network traces.
[03:10] Maya Chen: Who owns the experiment? Diego, you?
[03:13] Diego Ramos: Yep, Diego + Metrics team. we'll produce a dashboard and a short doc on methodology.
[03:18] Asha Kapoor: Ops will need the doc because we'll be asked to explain cost anomalies to customers.
[03:22] Speaker 2: quick HR move — can we confirm the hiring pause exceptions?
[03:27] Maya Chen: Yes, we're pausing general hiring but we have exemptions for infra and SRE roles. we want to keep the runway and also address incident frequency.
[03:36] Asha Kapoor: On rotations — holiday oncall is coming up, we propose a rotation that reduces any single person's block to two weeks and ensures a backstop shift.
[03:46] Ling Zhao: Also recommend a standby tier for critical customers on Dedicated during the holidays.
[03:51] Diego Ramos: From Product: tentative plan to offer a 'priority route' option in Dedicated — customers can pay a small premium for reserved warm caches. still exploratory.
[04:03] Samir Patel: That's interesting but dangerous if it fragments cache fairness. we need to ensure priority routes don't starve the rest.
[04:12] Maya Chen: We'll do a careful experiment, not a wide launch.
[04:18] Speaker 3: question from the chat — what about compliance docs? SOC2 re-audit timeline?
[04:24] Asha Kapoor: SOC 2 re-audit is on schedule, vendor side completed, auditor slot in November. we'll share the evidence pack next week.
[04:31] Ling Zhao: Also, small pedantic note — KMS integration test found a race in rotation logic; streaky but manageable. We'll patch it.
[04:40] Speaker 4: there was some confusion in the dev chat about 'Redwood dedicate' vs 'Redwood Dedicated' — ops pls clarify product naming in the docs.
[04:48] Diego Ramos: Noted; product will standardize naming across the console and docs.
[04:52] Maya Chen: Ok let's move to a short retrospective on the incident — Ling?
[04:56] Ling Zhao: Short version: multiple low-risk changes aligned and produced a higher-risk state. We'll run a blameless post-mortem, share the RCA publicly with leadership and extract 3 playbook changes.
[05:12] Samir Patel: One of those playbook changes is adding an orchestration guard around cache eviction. another is changing the scale-in policy to prefer draining non-critical shards first.
[05:26] Asha Kapoor: Ops will update runbooks and schedule tabletop exercises next week.
[05:31] Maya Chen: Hiring snapshot? Diego?
[05:33] Diego Ramos: We're still prioritizing infra, SRE and two senior infra engineers. product hires are frozen except for experiment leads.
[05:42] Speaker 5: question on Dedicated customer comms — do we preemptively inform affected customers before the next maintenance window?
[05:47] Diego Ramos: Yes, we'll prepare a heads-up that summarizes the blameless outcomes, changes and expected maintenance windows.
[05:53] Asha Kapoor: Ops will supply a template for that comms.
[05:56] Speaker 6: any updates on international regions?
[05:59] Samir Patel: We're testing a eu-west region POC with partner infra. Nothing to announce yet, but it's in internal staging.
[06:08] Ling Zhao: From SRE perspective, region replication tests were green aside from small cloud provider latency spikes. We'll keep monitoring.
[06:18] Maya Chen: OK going to the Q&A — remember to keep questions short.
[06:25] Speaker 7: are there changes to oncall compensation for holiday coverage?
[06:28] Asha Kapoor: We'll publish details; short answer yes, there will be enhanced comp for weekend coverage.
[06:33] Speaker 8: curious about metrics — what will we ship for per-route telemetry to customers?
[06:37] Diego Ramos: A two-phase rollout: phase one internal telemetry and dashboards, phase two limited beta with a group of customers on Dedicated.
[06:45] Samir Patel: We want to avoid any telemetry that touches the hot path. lightweight sampling and async aggregation.
[06:52] Speaker 9: can we get a status on the CLI overhaul?
[06:55] Diego Ramos: CLI v2 is in alpha, we'll put a canary binary out to core customers in November.
[07:02] Maya Chen: Any final asks?
[07:07] Asha Kapoor: Quick administrative — town halls will move to 10am pacific alternating weeks. ops will publish an invite.
[07:14] Ling Zhao: Blameless is set for Tuesday the 13th, postmortem notes to leadership by Friday.
[07:18] Samir Patel: Can I get an ops signal list for metrics to watch during the canary?
[07:22] Asha Kapoor: Yes, I'll send the list: head latencies, p95/p99 token latency, cpu% and KV cache miss rates.
[07:29] Speaker 10: will we change SLA language for Dedicated customers after this?
[07:33] Diego Ramos: We will propose minor clarifications — nothing that changes the current guarantees, mostly added exceptions and transparency language.
[07:40] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll close with the three asks: publish holiday rotation calendar, run blameless + RCA, and Diego to share telemetry timeline.
[07:50] Speaker 11: thanks, see you all.

End of meeting.

Notes about transcript quality: auto-generated; occasional mis-hear of technical terms ("KV cash" vs "KV cache", "Redwood dedicate" vs "Redwood Dedicated"). Some speaker labels replaced by generic "Speaker X" for audience questions.
